attack: The strongest opposing bundle is trend-follower plus dollar-king: US 2Y is still cheapening after a delivered hike (+9bp 1d, +57bp 1m, 100th percentile), G10 tightening is broadening, so USD stays bid and CAD/NZD stay offered, making a 2s10s steepener a premature fade. That smuggles three claims that the packet does not jointly support. First, paying US 2Y is not USD-up and is not a mandate to keep flattening 2s10s; trend-follower already says a flattener is the wrong rates expression because term premium can lift 10s. Second, USD-up as a growth-scare needs confirmation in activity, credit and vol; ISM Services 55.4, payrolls +162k, retail +1.2%, VIX 15.44, HY OAS 270bp and copper at the 92nd percentile are the opposite confirmation. Third, CAD-lower and NZD-lower are leftover USD-pair tags on already-extended USDCAD and already-washed NZDUSD, contradicted by Canada cyclical leadership and an NZ GDP beat, and by dollar-king's own refusal to fade CAD inside AUDCAD. AU-duration doves tagging USD higher, and rate-hawk tagging USD higher while receiving US 5Y, are synopsis inconsistencies, not competing owners of this curve discrepancy.
defense: The trade is a duration-neutral US 2s10s steepener, not long 2Y duration, not short AUDUSD, and not a chase of cheap NZDUSD. USD-lower is the implication that a hiking-into-slowdown flatten overshot resilient growth, so the extra hike premium in 2s should stop leading 10s; it is not a spot-USD short versus AUD housing. CAD-higher and NZD-higher remain supporting cyclical reads, expressed in the US curve because NZ official yields are blocked and USDCAD's rates residual is weak. CA-US 5Y is the nearest rates alternative and is left as runner-up: it owns a policy-gap RV, not the growth-scare mispricing. AUD-lower is already conceded to the housing channel and is not this seat's expression. Unchanged because the opposing USD/CAD/NZD flags do not falsify the curve discrepancy and do not offer a cleaner pro-growth rates expression.
holes_in_opposing_case: USD-higher is a synopsis overlay, not a shared instrument: dollar-king shorts AUDUSD, trend-follower pays US 2Y, rate-hawk receives US 5Y versus Canada, and mean-reverter/rate-dove/perma-bear receive AU duration. Those trades do not jointly own a still-live USD growth-scare bid.

The post-hike USD premium is already paid in the pairs the USD-up camp cites: NZDUSD -3.90% 1m at the 8.6th 5y percentile, USDCAD +1.74% 1m at the 87th 5y percentile, EURUSD -1.89%, GBPUSD -2.07%. Tagging NZD and CAD still lower is extrapolation of a completed USD-pair move, not unpaid tightening.

Trend-follower's pay-US-2Y case does not imply CAD lower or a continuing 2s10s flatten. Their own thesis says term-premium/BoE QT can lift the long end even as 2s cheapen, which is a steepener if 10s lead on the way up, and they already reject a 2s10s flattener. Long USDCAD as the spot analog fights 140bp 2Y USD-over-CAD carry, a weak USDCAD vs CA-US 2Y residual (r-squared 0.022), and Canada activity 53.2 / Q2 GDP +0.8% q/q versus US activity 49.92.

Dollar-king's CAD-lower and NZD-lower tags contradict their AUDUSD rationale: they refused AUDCAD specifically because an implicit CAD long would import oil, BoC energy pass-through, and stronger Canadian activity 53.2 / consumer 52.5. That is an admission CAD is cyclically supported, then they marked CAD lower anyway as USD residue.

Perma-bear's USD-up / NZD-down is an Australia-housing risk-off overlay. Receive AU 2Y can be locally right while US ISM Services 55.4, payrolls +162k, August retail +1.2%, VIX 15.44, HY OAS 270bp and copper at the 92nd percentile still refuse a growth accident. Citing those same complacent risk prints as evidence the break has not happened is the bull case, not confirmation NZD should extend a 3.90% 1m wash after a Q2 GDP beat.

Mean-reverter and rate-dove tag USD higher while receiving AU 10Y/2Y. That USD flag is unowned: AU duration rally is not a USD-up expression. Mean-reverter even considered long US 2s10s and rejected it because the flatten is the same fully priced Fed hike, which concedes the hiking event is known information already sitting in 2s10s at 25bp, 1y percentile 0.2%, -21bp 1m.

Rate-hawk tags USD higher while the selected trade receives US 5Y in CA-US 5Y RV. Receiving 99th-percentile US 5Y after a >90% priced, delivered 25bp hike is a USD-rates-down expression. Their CAD-higher view agrees with this seat; CA-US 5Y remains a 150-175bp policy-gap RV (Fed 3.75-4.00% vs BoC 2.25%), not the growth-versus-recession discrepancy in US curve shape.

expression_comparison.rates_candidate: Duration-neutral US 2s10s steepener: receive UST 2Y versus pay UST 10Y. Packet print is 25bp on 2026-09-18, 1y percentile 0.2% / z_1y -2.45 after a -21bp 1m flatten (z -2.20). Alternative considered: long CA-US 5Y (pay CA 5Y / receive US 5Y) at -124bp, 1y percentile 0.2% and 5y percentile 6.9%.
expression_comparison.rationale: Rates are preferred because the growth-versus-recession discrepancy lives in curve shape, not in a cheap FX level. US 2s10s owns that gap directly after a fully priced 25bp hike, while NZDUSD mixes an energy-importer shock, unavailable NZ yields, and weak NZ labor (47.0). USDCAD is inferior because the packet's USDCAD vs CA-US 2Y residual is weak (r-squared 0.022) and 140bp 2Y carry favors USD over CAD. CA-US 5Y is a strong RV but is closer to the existing 150-175bp policy-rate gap (Fed 3.75-4.00% vs BoC 2.25%) than to a growth mispricing. NZ-involved rate RV is unavailable.
expression_comparison.spot_candidate: Long NZDUSD (spot 0.5711, 5y percentile 8.6%, -3.90% 1m) as the cheapest cyclical USD pair after NZ Q2 GDP +0.2% q/q beat forecasts; runner-up short USDCAD on Canada activity 53.2 versus US 49.92.

revised_trade.horizon: 4-8 weeks; post-hike data and next inflation/labor prints to test whether the 1m flatten was a growth scare or a completed hiking event
revised_trade.invalidation: ISM Services or manufacturing fall into contraction, payrolls and unemployment break materially weaker, and HY OAS/VIX reprice a growth accident while 2s10s keeps flattening. A 5y-window confirmation that 25bp is a normal curve in this hiking regime without a growth rebound would also downgrade the stretch argument.
revised_trade.mispricing: US 2s10s at 25bp (1y percentile 0.2%, 1m -21bp) prices a hiking-into-slowdown path that is not confirmed by expansionary ISM services, stable labor, tight HY, low VIX, or high copper. The 5y 2s10s percentile of 54% means this is a change/1y-distribution discrepancy, not a 5y cheapness claim. Credit-equity-survey triangulation says the recession flattening overshot.
principal_risks: Energy shock absorbers weaken further and a genuine stagflation hit validates the flatten; BoC already flags fuel pass-through and Shell/Equinor warn buffers are thinner.
US consumer remains the soft spot: temperature 48.5, Michigan preliminary September 47.8 (-7.5% m/m), Q2 GDP +1.5% SAAR versus +2.1% in Q1.
The 5y 2s10s percentile is 54%, so 1y-window extremes can persist if this hiking regime has a lower curve mean; mean reversion is a yardstick, not the signal.
Another hawkish Fed or upside CPI surprise can extend bear-flattening if 2Y cheapens faster than 10Y; August CPI already kept the tightening bias intact.

Australian housing (stamp duty -24% y/y, prices more than 7% off peak) is a real regional growth hole; this trade does not own that, but a broader commodity risk-off could still flatten UST via a global scare.
Positioning, dealer balance sheet and executable levels are unknown; paper books are empty and Cot/flow is a known gap.
revised_trade.structure: Duration-neutral 2s10s steepener: receive US 2Y versus pay US 10Y. Equal-yield weights are not claimed; packet notes 2s5s10s is equal-yield, not DV01-neutral. No executable structure or size is in the packet.
revised_trade.thesis: FACT: The Fed delivered the widely priced 25bp hike to 3.75-4.00%; futures had assigned greater than 90% odds before the meeting. US 2Y is 4.76% (1y percentile 99.8%, +57bp 1m) and US 10Y is 5.01% (1y percentile 99.6%, +36bp 1m), leaving 2s10s at 25bp. That spread's 252-observation percentile is 0.0 with z -2.49, 1y percentile 0.2% / z_1y -2.45, and a -21bp 1m change (z -2.20); 5s10s is 15bp with 1y percentile 0.4%. FACT: Hard US data are not collapsing. Unemployment is 4.1% unchanged; payrolls +162k with positive revisions; ISM Services 55.4 with business activity and new orders above 60; ISM Manufacturing 54.6 still expansionary; August retail sales +1.2% m/m after July was revised to -0.5%. FACT: Risk markets are not pricing a growth accident: VIX 15.44 (14.7th percentile), HY OAS 270bp (13.7th percentile), S&P 500 7638 (90th percentile, +1.13% 1d), copper 6.59 (92nd percentile). Canada Q2 GDP +0.8% q/q and activity temperature 53.2 are the strongest cyclical prints in the four-country set; NZ Q2 GDP +0.2% q/q beat forecasts. INFERENCE: The 1m bear-flattening is the market's slowdown tax on a hike that was already in the price. If growth and risk appetite remain resilient, 2s should stop cheapening versus 10s: either the additional-hike premium in 2s fades now that September is delivered, or term yields stay bid with activity and the curve re-steepens. The desk line that domestic growth is softer is the over-discounted pessimism. UNKNOWN: Next-meeting hike odds are not in the packet; positioning/flow is unavailable; NZ yields are blocked so NZ growth cannot be expressed in rates; 5y 2s10s percentile is 54%, so the flattening is extreme only on the 1y window.
why_now: The Sep 16 hike is done and had been greater than 90% priced, so further flattening now has to come from a genuine growth scare rather than from delivering a known FOMC outcome.
US 2s10s just printed the 0th percentile of the 252-observation opportunity screen and 1y percentile 0.2% after a statistically large 1m flatten.
Same-week triangulation is still expansionary: ISM Services 55.4, August retail +1.2%, payrolls +162k, VIX 15.44, HY OAS 270bp, copper at the 92nd percentile.
Canada and NZ growth prints (CA GDP +0.8% q/q; NZ GDP beat at +0.2% q/q) argue the global cyclical complex is not rolling over even as the desk narrative leans softer growth.
Saudi ship-to-ship workaround and modest oil easing reduce the extreme left tail that would justify a lasting curve collapse, even though energy shock absorbers remain a risk.

strongest_opposing_claim: Trend-follower and dollar-king: post-FOMC US 2Y is still cheapening after a delivered, previously >90% priced hike, G10 tightening is broadening, so USD stays bid, CAD and NZD stay offered, and fading the 100th-percentile front end via a 2s10s steepener is premature mean reversion.
uncertainty: Next-meeting hike odds are not in the packet; 5y 2s10s percentile is 54% so the extreme is 1y-window only; NZ official yields are blocked; positioning/flow and executable levels are unavailable; energy shock absorbers and US consumer 48.5 / Michigan 47.8 remain live left tails.
what_would_concede: ISM Services or manufacturing fall into contraction, payrolls and unemployment break materially weaker, and HY OAS/VIX reprice a growth accident while 2s10s keeps flattening because 2Y continues to lead 10Y higher. A 5y-window confirmation that 25bp is a normal curve in this hiking regime without a growth rebound would also concede the stretch argument.
